long-hours.name: Long hours
long-hours.line: I work so many hours that there's barely any of my life left.

sources.passage: 10% of employees in the OECD work 50 hours or more per week in paid work.
745 000 deaths from stroke and ischemic heart disease in 2016
currently stands at 9% of the total population globally

long-hours.prevalence: 10% of employees in OECD countries work 50 hours or more a week; 9% of the world's population works long hours, and long hours caused 745 000 deaths from stroke and heart disease in 2016 (WHO and ILO).

unpredictable-schedule.name: Schedule
unpredictable-schedule.line: My work hours change so often that I can't plan my life.

sources.passage: 60% receive their work schedules less than two weeks in advance; 73% report irregular or variable work schedules; 45% worked consecutive closing/opening shifts (“clopenings”)
2.8 million on-call workers (1.7 percent of total employment)

unpredictable-schedule.prevalence: Among Boston service workers, 60% get their schedules less than two weeks ahead, 73% have irregular or variable schedules and 45% worked a closing shift followed by an opening shift (Shift Project); 2.8 million U.S. workers are on call (1.7 percent of employment, BLS).

unsafe-work.name: Unsafe work
unsafe-work.line: I could get badly hurt doing my job.

sources.passage: Private industry employers reported 2.5 million nonfatal workplace injuries and illnesses in 2024
There were 5,070 fatal work injuries recorded in the United States in 2024

unsafe-work.prevalence: U.S. private employers reported 2.5 million nonfatal workplace injuries and illnesses in 2024, and 5,070 people died from work injuries that year (BLS).

wage-theft.name: Wage theft
wage-theft.line: My boss doesn't pay me everything I've earned.

sources.passage: The report says this form of wage theft affects 17 percent of low-wage workers.
In the 10 most populous U.S. states, 2.4 million workers lose $8 billion annually to minimum wage violations

wage-theft.prevalence: 17 percent of low-wage workers are paid less than the minimum wage; in the 10 most populous states that is 2.4 million workers losing $8 billion a year (Economic Policy Institute, via Next City).

bad-boss.name: Bad boss
bad-boss.line: My boss makes my job miserable.

sources.passage: Gallup surveyed over 7,000 members of the US workforce and found that half of them have left a job at some point in their careers solely because they could no longer put up with their manager.
Their relationship with their manager or supervisor (59%)

bad-boss.prevalence: Half of more than 7,000 U.S. workers have left a job at some point to get away from their manager (Gallup); 59% are highly satisfied with their relationship with their manager (Pew).

no-say-at-work.name: No say at work
no-say-at-work.line: I have no say in how things are done at work.

sources.passage: 48% of nonunion workers said they would vote for a union if an election was held at their workplace.

no-say-at-work.prevalence: 48% of U.S. nonunion workers say they would vote for a union if an election were held at their workplace (MIT Sloan survey, via Cornell ILR).

overqualified.name: Overqualified
overqualified.line: My job doesn't use what I know or what I trained for.

sources.passage: More than half of recent four-year college graduates, 52 percent, are underemployed a year after they graduate
one in four, or 1.9 million individuals, were either underemployed or unemployed.

overqualified.prevalence: 52 percent of recent four-year college graduates are underemployed a year after graduating (Burning Glass Institute and Strada); one in four college-educated immigrants in the U.S., 1.9 million people, were underemployed or unemployed (Migration Policy Institute).

long-commute.name: Commute
long-commute.line: I lose hours every day getting to and from work.

sources.passage: About 8.1 percent of U.S. workers have commutes of 60 minutes or longer.
The average time spent commuting in the U.S. in 2023 was about 27 minutes one-way

long-commute.prevalence: About 8.1 percent of U.S. workers commute 60 minutes or longer each way (Census Bureau); the average one-way commute was about 27 minutes in 2023 (NCSL, from Census data).

no-paid-leave.name: Paid leave
no-paid-leave.line: I lose pay whenever I'm sick or need to care for someone.
aliases: Can't afford to stay home sick

sources.passage: 81 percent had access to paid sick leave
49 percent had access to paid family and medical leave

no-paid-leave.prevalence: 81 percent of U.S. private industry workers had access to paid sick leave and 49 percent to paid family and medical leave (BLS).

gig-work.name: Gig work
gig-work.line: I work through apps with no benefits and no steady pay.

sources.passage: In total, 9% of U.S. adults are current or recent gig workers.
In July 2023, 4.3 percent of workers--6.9 million people--held contingent jobs on their sole or main job
35% say they have often or sometimes felt unsafe while doing these jobs

gig-work.prevalence: 9% of U.S. adults are current or recent gig platform workers, and 35% of gig workers have often or sometimes felt unsafe on the job (Pew); 4.3 percent of workers, 6.9 million people, hold contingent jobs (BLS, July 2023).

two-jobs.name: Second job
two-jobs.line: I work more than one job just to get by.

sources.passage: Multiple Jobholders as a Percent of Employed: Sep 2026: 5.5 | Percent, Seasonally Adjusted

two-jobs.prevalence: 5.5 percent of employed Americans hold more than one job (BLS via FRED, Sep 2026).

small-business.name: My business
small-business.line: I'm struggling to keep my small business going.

sources.passage: Small Business Credit Survey: Experienced at Least One Financial Challenge: Employer Firms: 94 percent (2025)

small-business.prevalence: 94 percent of small employer firms faced at least one financial challenge in the past year (Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey, 2025).

dead-end-job.name: Dead end
dead-end-job.line: I can't move up at work, however hard I try.

sources.passage: about a quarter (26%) are highly satisfied with their opportunities for promotion at work.

dead-end-job.prevalence: Only about a quarter of U.S. workers (26%) are highly satisfied with their opportunities for promotion (Pew).
